correctness.rationale: A circular word with positive counts (a,b,c) induces an Eulerian undirected multigraph with three labeled vertices, loop counts h_ii and symmetric off-diagonal multiplicities x,y,z. Vertex degrees 2a,2b,2c require x,y,z all share one parity; parameterization x=2i+delta,y=2j+delta,z=2k+delta with nonnegative loops yields exactly G=(1+tuv)/[(1-t)(1-u)(1-v)(1-tu)(1-tv)(1-uv)]. At positive compositions only the all-loop case and exactly one positive cross-edge type are disconnected: subtract 1+min(a,b)+min(a,c)+min(b,c). Euler's circuit theorem gives a constructive inverse preserving half-degrees and exact counts. Summing integer triples at a=b=c=m gives m(m²+3m-2)/2. The zero-error capacity is the number of outputs by one representative word per distinct image. Independent exhaustive circular-word histogram enumerations checked every positive composition at lengths 3 through 8 (56 cases) and balanced evaluations for m through 7.
